items.question: Why does LINE rely on random walks to capture second-order proximity, and how does that choice help it scale to millions of nodes?
items.false_premise: LINE uses random walks to capture second-order proximity.
items.correction: LINE does not use random walks; it optimizes an objective that preserves local and global network structures, including first-order and second-order proximity.
items.evidence_quote: In this paper, we propose such a network embedding model called the “LINE,” which is able to scale to very large, arbitrary types of networks: undirected, directed and/or weighted.

items.question: How does LINE preserve only first-order proximity while ignoring global network structure, and why is that sufficient for real-world graphs?
items.false_premise: LINE preserves only first-order proximity and ignores global network structure.
items.correction: LINE optimizes an objective which preserves both the local and global network structures.
items.evidence_quote: The model optimizes an objective which preserves both the local and global network structures.

items.question: What makes LINE depend on observed links as the sole signal for global similarity, given that it treats second-order proximity as determined by edge weights?
items.false_premise: LINE treats second-order proximity as determined by edge weights and uses observed links as the sole signal for global similarity.
items.correction: LINE says second-order proximity is not determined through the observed tie strength but through the shared neighborhood structures of the vertices.
items.evidence_quote: As a complement, we explore the second-order proximity between the vertices, which is not determined through the observed tie strength but through the shared neighborhood structures of the vertices.

items.question: Under which conditions does LINE work only for undirected, unweighted networks, unlike methods designed for directed graphs?
items.false_premise: LINE works only for undirected, unweighted networks.
items.correction: LINE is able to scale to very large, arbitrary types of networks, including undirected, directed and/or weighted networks.
items.evidence_quote: In this paper, we propose such a network embedding model called the “LINE,” which is able to scale to very large, arbitrary types of networks: undirected, directed and/or weighted.
